column5: Layered gabbro, norite and anorthosite; a basic to ultrabasic intrusion forming the Freetown peninsula hills
column6: Massive and crystalline, with negligible primary porosity. Groundwater is confined to the weathered mantle and to fracture and joint sets; yields are modest and highly site-dependent, so the fracture target is the whole of the siting problem

column5: Unconsolidated to poorly consolidated sands, clays, clayey sands and lignite, with beach sand and alluvium; estuarine and deltaic
column6: Intergranular. The most productive ground in the country for its thickness, but the coastal strip carries a real risk of saline intrusion and of shallow contamination, because the same porosity that stores water passes it

column5: Sands, clays, clayey sands and lignite over the coastal lowland; alluvium along the drainage
column6: Intergranular, generally the best yields available without deep drilling. Shallow water tables mean the protective cover is thin, so siting must keep clear of latrines and surface drainage

column4: Precambrian basement: migmatitic gneiss and granitoid, Leonean and Liberian granite, migmatites and hybrid rocks
column5: Crystalline basement - granite, granitoid, gneiss and migmatite, with metagabbro and amphibolite bodies
column6: The classic crystalline basement aquifer this toolkit is built for: no primary porosity, water in the weathered and fractured zone above fresh rock. Yield follows regolith thickness and the fracture set at the weathered-fresh contact

column5: Metasediments - sandstone, siltstone, shale and conglomerate, with the Kasewe volcanic member
column6: Fracture flow in the indurated members; the shales are aquicludes rather than aquifers. Yields vary sharply over short distances, so a sounding at the wellhead is worth more here than anywhere else

column6: A dyke is usually a barrier rather than an aquifer, but its margins are commonly fractured and its contact with the country rock can concentrate flow. The dyke itself is the wrong target; the contact beside it may be the right one
